observations: All 3 alpha_prior values (0.5, 1.0, 2.0) pass both C1 (null median < 0) and C3 (p=0.0005 < 0.001). This is the first estimator family to simultaneously pass both criteria across the full alpha sweep on this SPA class.

The corrected K=12 null median of -78 to -131 nats (depending on alpha) is well-centered negative, confirming Occam's razor correctly penalizes the larger action-dependent model under the null. The parent's K=len(counts) bug produced +3700 to +4000 nats upward bias, entirely explained by the single-line error.

The observed log Bayes factors (168-643 nats at alpha 2.0-0.5) are large and well-separated from the null distribution maximum (-21 to -93 nats depending on alpha). The gap between observed and 99.9th percentile is 194-669 nats across alphas, demonstrating robust sensitivity.

Deterministic SPA positive control produces log BF 854-916 nats, confirming the Bayesian implementation correctly detects strong action effects. The stochastic SPA signal (168-643 nats) is 19-75% of the deterministic ceiling, consistent with 50% stochasticity.

Phase 2 beyond-Markov: K3-K2 = 235 nats at alpha=0.5 (point estimate positive), but bootstrap CI [-415, 34] includes zero, indicating high variance in the K3-K2 difference across bootstrap resamples. Phase 2 is exploratory per the frozen spec and does not gate the main verdict.

Stratum size decomposition: 343 strata in 5-9 bucket (2147 records) and 37 strata in 10-19 bucket (433 records). No strata with >=20 records, indicating the N=5000 dataset produces many small strata. Both buckets show significant positive log BF (188 and 68 nats respectively).

The parent experiment EXP-PHYSICS-35572180485 MEASUREMENT_INVALID verdict was entirely due to the K=len(counts) bug. With corrected K=12, the same data and shuffle framework yield SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST. The audit-corrected recomputation (null median -78 to -131 nats) is confirmed by this independent frozen re-execution.

The log BF scale (nats) is fundamentally different from the PMI/CMI scale (bits) used in prior estimator families. The Bayesian approach operates on marginal likelihood ratio, not direct CMI estimation, which explains why it succeeds where plug-in KL, entropy-rate, KSG, and LR chi2 all failed.
validity_notes: All evidence is synthetic SPA simulation. C-WEB-DYNAMICS concerns real Web dynamics. This experiment validates the Bayesian estimator paradigm on a controlled synthetic testbed, not on production Web data.

The Bayes factor operates on nats scale (natural logarithm), not bits. The null distribution is centered at -78 to -131 nats (depending on alpha), not near zero. The decision criteria (median < 0, p < 0.001) are adapted for this scale.
N_SHUFFLE=1999 achieves minimum achievable p=0.0005, well below the 0.001 threshold. The p-value is exact (no interpolation needed).

The stratum size distribution is skewed: 343 strata have 5-9 records, 37 have 10-19 records. No strata with >=20 records exist at N=5000, suggesting that larger N would improve stratum-level estimation.

Phase 2 beyond-Markov K3-K2 testing is exploratory. The bootstrap CI for K3-K2 includes zero despite the point estimate being positive (235 nats). This high variance may reflect limited within-session action diversity or the interaction between history conditioning and stratum fragmentation.

The positive control (deterministic SPA) produces log BF 854-916 nats, confirming the implementation detects strong signals. The stochastic SPA produces 168-643 nats (19-75% of deterministic ceiling), consistent with the 50% stochastic mixing ratio.
The Dirichlet-Multinomial marginal likelihood is a closed-form computation; no MCMC or variational inference is needed. Numerical stability is maintained via log-space computation (math.lgamma).

The within-session shuffle preserves session structure, state sequence, and url_before/url_after pairing while randomizing action labels. This is the correct null for testing action-dependent structure.
